newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets raid south Lebanon guerrilla targets.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets raid south Lebanon guerrilla targets.

text.p: Israeli warplanes attacked suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon after nightfall on Wednesday after launching similar raids in the morning, Lebanese security sources said.

They said two planes fired four air-to-surface rockets shortly after nightfall into the Iqlim al-Toufah ridge which is controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
There was no immediate word on casualties. Israeli planes also rocketed Hizbollah targets on the ridge three times in the early morning. No casualties were reported then.
Earlier Hizbollah guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the Israeli outpost of Blat on the edge of Israel's occupation zone, causing no casualties, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
They said Israeli gunners fired back at Lebanese-held areas facing the outpost. No casualties were reported.
Commenting on the earlier raids, a Hizbollah spokesman in Beirut said the Israeli raids targeted areas around the villages of Louwaizeh and Iqmata in Iqlim al-Toufah at around 6:30 a.m. (0430 GMT).
The air raids were the first into Lebanon since Sunday, when Israeli aircraft struck at Hizbollah targets in southeast Lebanon after a clash between Israeli troops and Moslem guerrillas.

A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon said on Tuesday at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel on Friday night. The group did not reprimand Lebanon.
The rocket was the first fired at northern Israel since a ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April that killed some 200 people, mostly civilians.
Hizbollah, which fired volleys of Katyushas at Israel before the ceasefire, has denied responsibility for the latest rocket attack.
